scope.description: Static local-state and transition-type census. Current HTTP ingest-v2 SourceActor through initial Publisher, detached batch uploads and IndexingPipeline. Common execution and actor mechanics are recorded once.
scope.count_rule: Sum states minus shared_states per graph. Sum unique edge triples per graph, including owner-qualified dependency enter/wakeup edges and guarded self-loops with real effects. No multiplication by actors, tasks, shards, batches, permits or queue slots. This is a parameterized inventory, not a reachable global-state count. Numeric values, IDs, nesting depths, collection contents and error payloads remain parameters.
scope.shared_rule: Every shared_states entry names a state defined without that marker in a common graph. Shared endpoints are anchors only. Their generic execution/dispatch transitions are not copied. A wait-to-ready edge means wake/enabling notification, not completed acquisition. Actual future completion is observed during a subsequent poll. Immediate-ready completion uses the explicitly listed running self-loop. Source and supervisor unbounded sends have no capacity-wait state.
scope.runtime_offload: offload_pending means the caller has returned Pending awaiting blocking filesystem work. It is a specialization of pending, disjoint from pending-other in this abstraction. Blocking-pool scheduling internals are excluded. No indexing actor CPU loop is reclassified as spawn_blocking.
scope.dependency_evidence: Tokio 1.53.1 from quickwit/Cargo.lock#L10692-L10695. Cached dependency source inspected: tokio-1.53.1/src/fs/mod.rs lines 9-21 and src/fs/remove_dir_all.rs lines 11-14 confirm filesystem spawn_blocking. Repository call sites are cited below.

exclusions: WAL, ingest router, persist/replication, fetch server and fetch client/helper tasks, MultiFetchStream internal queues/retry/reconnect, and after-Source detached truncation RPC/retry tasks.

All alternate Source implementations, including ingest-v1, Kafka, Kinesis, file/stdin, queue, Pulsar and Pub/Sub. SourceActor wrapper paths selectable only for those sources are not counted as current ingest-v2 waits.
Merge internals. Initial Publisher's optional capacity-1 NewSplits notification is retained as a boundary dependency only. Shared cache/startup contention is noted without importing merge graphs.

Intrinsic Tantivy/docstore compression worker, storage SDK/S3, metastore DB/transaction internals, network protocol, filesystem/OS and executor/blocking-pool internals. Explicit synchronous blocking and tokio filesystem offload caller states are retained once.
Concurrent ingesthree async wrapper edits and all uncommitted changes are outside committed audit snapshot. No repository files are edited.

No CPU time bound, per-function phase expansion, batch/task/queue-slot bound, global product graph, BFS, all-interleaving count, or complexity percentage. Counters, positions, tokens, errors, collection sizes, protection depth and retry count remain parameters.

Defensive Source subscribe-error and unexpected post-EOF payload/error transitions are not claimed reachable from normal helper contracts. Normal assigned-shard paths are enumerated, defensive alternatives remain unresolved.

Supervisor source-load wait/NotFound branches belonging to other configured sources are omitted from ingest-v2-specific counts. IngestSource::try_new performs synchronous construction despite its async signature.
No capacity wait for Source self-loop, Publisher SuggestTruncate/ordered Source exit, or supervisor AssignShards: Source mailbox is unbounded. These sends do not wait for handling.
Per-message generic reply-oneshot/ask machinery beyond the retained Sequencer result reservation is excluded: stage senders discard reply receivers and do not await replies.

Exact queue occupancy states, byte-gauge values and cache registry/quota reconciliation are not expanded. Capacity admission gates and message custody/stashed-envelope state preserve the relevant actor-level boundaries.

Filesystem cleanup failures and uncertain RPC outcomes are not converted into successful deletion/rollback. Remote durable effects are separately projected, not inferred from an error response. Process crash recovery/GC is outside these actors.
counting_rule: Count graph-local states excluding shared_states. Count distinct (from,to) edges with from != to; alternative triggers and unchanged-state retries do not add edges. Shared runtime counted once per design, actor framework once for current only. No global products or execution counts.

edges: future returns Pending on a dependency other than filesystem offload
explicit yield_now self-wakes and returns Pending
synchronous IO, contended synchronous lock or blocking IO limiter holds the polling thread
synchronous operation returns on the same polling thread
tokio filesystem operation submits blocking work and its join future returns Pending
filesystem offload completion wakes its caller
awaited future is immediately Ready and the same poll continues
graphs.notes: Initial state for a spawned task is ready. Waking is not immediate execution. Kill-switch death does not create pending-to-terminal or thread-blocked-to-terminal edges. Source is NonBlocking. Processor, Indexer, Serializer and Packager are persistent async tasks on the Blocking Tokio runtime, not dedicated threads or per-message offloads. Other actors and detached uploads inherit the spawning runtime. OS descheduling and dependency worker internals are excluded.

actor_running means queue-consumption permission, independent of execution.running. Outer receive selects both queues when running and high only when paused. Inner drain tests mode once before entering, so Pause dispatched inside drain does not prevent remaining low messages in that drain. High priority never interrupts a handler. Real panic can bypass ctx.exit and leave this atomic mode unchanged.

edges: remove envelope then perform pre-handler kill/yield checks and invoke handler
handler returns Ok; resume receive/drain policy
running drain loop explicitly yielded and inbox is still empty
hook returns Ok and mailbox-lifetime check permits continuation
handler or dispatched command returns exit status
last external mailbox absent and inbox empty at completion check
finalize returns; record fault if applicable and publish atomic exit state
graphs.notes: These are framework dispatch/lifecycle obligations, not per-function CPU phases. Hooks may run without suspending. Source initialize directly calls its first Loop. Framework optional yields occur at outer-loop entry and before each handler. Source, Processor and Indexer disable those optional yields. Drain-probe yield remains for all actors. Actual panic skips normal finalize/ctx.exit. Drop collects observation, join reports Panicked.

cooperative kill check observes dead switch
task unwinds before an exit status was selected
graphs.notes: Outcome is separate from atomic ActorState. Only Success maps to actor_success. Normal Failure, DownstreamClosed and returned Panicked activate the generation switch. Quit and Killed do not activate it themselves. Generic outcomes are recorded once rather than appended to every owner graph.

high or low envelope arrival wakes receive

command or scheduled high-priority envelope wakes receive
eligible envelope is already available and receive completes immediately
graphs.notes: Protected receive mechanics shared once by all eight stages and supervisor. Source fetch-next and Sequencer result waits are owner-specific handler dependencies below. Low arrival alone does not unblock a paused outer receive. Actor context owns a mailbox, so ordinary sender disconnection is not an additional input-failure state.

send fails on receiver closure and pipeline caller drops payload

graphs.notes: One envelope, independent of queue length and task execution. Bounded(0) has no resident low queue, but pending sender retains payload. The extra saved low envelope is outside capacity. Message admission returns a reply receiver; these pipeline sends do not await handler replies. Owner-qualified capacity gates are counted below, not duplicated here as generic waits.

edges: timer callback attempts high-priority delivery and drops mailbox clone
graphs.notes: Applies to Indexer CommitTimeout/Resume and supervisor Spawn/SuperviseLoop. Enqueued envelope follows shared_envelope_ownership. Expiry is not handler preemption. Stale commit timers retain references and are not cancelled on early workbench extraction. No separate executor scheduling state is invented for the actor timer service.

nested guard enters or exits, retaining positive protection count
graphs.notes: Protection depth is a parameter, not an arbitrary bounded expansion. Protected waits can stay healthy indefinitely. Progress records do not yield. Detached uploads clone the uploader context; actor health is not a per-upload progress guarantee.

edges: kill, kill_with_fault or parent kill propagates to child
repeated kill preserves dead state and first fault semantics
graphs.notes: A fresh generation allocates a new switch, never resurrects this one. Handle kill adds Nudge and awaits join. The atomic/tree signal alone does not interrupt CPU, cancel RPCs or abort detached tasks. Fault contents are parameters.

Unchanged set returns before reacquisition. subscribe, ingest-v2 construction, and Source-local truncate have no internal IO await, so they introduce no source-task wait state.

Listed normal protocol paths avoid inventing late payloads after terminal EOF. Source has defensive subscribe-error and post-EOF error branches; reachability from normal helper contracts is unresolved and those additional transitions are excluded from totals. Missing acquisitions stay unassigned. Source-local completion is included, spawned truncate RPC/retry work is excluded.

graphs.notes: Protected wait retains processed documents, or a lock envelope after local replacement, or the finalization obligation. Raw processing is one synchronous loop with per-document protection and progress records. Invalid documents are dropped but checkpoint still advances. Dead publish lock discards at batch entry. No separate parse/map/VRL CPU phases or per-document yields are counted. Abnormal finalization skips ordered exit.

Synchronous add_document loop has no per-document await. Optional cooperative configuration removes permit edges at runtime, not the declared static branch.

Initial zero-builder construction and synchronous checkpoint extension stay in the same ownership state. Source emits only nonempty checkpoint deltas in this scope; the helper's empty-checkpoint no-output guard is documented without inventing an additional construction phase. Flush guards are memory target, document target, force_commit, matching timeout, cooperative drained hook and Success/Quit finalization. They share an ownership edge. Noncontiguous checkpoint fails the actor. Counter/checkpoint values remain parameters; empty/reset paths do not all reset counters.

No packaging sub-function states are invented.

Semaphore closure is not performed in this scope; expect/context defensive branch is not an additional invented transition.

Uploader resumes mailbox dispatch independently and default finalization does not join uploads. No task kill-select or universal abort barrier. Result can remain in later oneshot after permit release. This is ownership, not an invented upload-task CPU phase.

Remote put includes asynchronous reading of local split files. No task-local retry loop. Dead publish lock check occurs during preparation, not before each later await. Stage failure drops unresolved sender. Storage/cache/remove failure explicitly kill_with_fault. Dependency-internal retries and blocking-pool jobs remain outside scope.

Constructor may start in either state. Once disconnected this Publisher has no reconnect message. Presence controls whether success must attempt planner notification.

graphs.notes: Actual fixed three-attempt policy, not an audit-selected retry bound. States distinguish allowed next retry delay and exhaustion action. Delay execution is in publisher_handler_dependencies. Token is reloaded on every attempt.

edges: Source reset or exhausted-token Publisher acquires mutex then stores false
graphs.notes: One lock identity. Initial Source lock starts dead, reset allocates a different alive identity. No dead-to-alive resurrection. New identity travels Source -> Processor -> Indexer -> split messages. Processor checks at batch entry, Indexer after workbench creation, Packager per split, upload task during preparation, Publisher after mutex acquisition. Serializer has no check. Lock death fences publication independently of pipeline kill.

Source or terminating Publisher acquires kill mutex

graphs.notes: Mutex ownership controls another actor's enabled acquisition. Killer ownership is a synchronous critical section, not an invented suspension. Publisher ownership spans RPC and retry sleep, so Source reset can wait for publication.

edges: Source acquire_shards succeeds then ArcSwap stores plan-derived token
assignment adds shards; successful reacquisition stores token for all desired shards
graphs.notes: Shared ArcSwapOption is not an async mutex. Value/identity is a parameter. Supervisor retains the shared cell across generation restarts. Source reset does not clear it. Unchanged shard set returns before token renewal. Metastore request publication validation is an external conditional-transaction boundary, not a distributed-consensus graph.

edges: metastore accepts conditional publish_splits with checkpoint and token
graphs.notes: External effect projection of initial-indexing calls, not metastore internals. Stage precedes put. Publish follows completed uploads and FIFO sequencing. RPC failure does not prove absence of remote effects. No reverse/rollback edge is implemented by these actors. Deletion/GC and merge replacement are excluded.

edges: remote storage put completes the split object
graphs.notes: Remote object fact independent of staged metadata and publication. Cache/removal/publication failure can leave object stored. S3 multipart/upload internals and object cleanup are outside scope. RPC failure knowledge is not conflated with actual object absence.

edges: accepted publish_splits applies checkpoint delta, including EmptySplit with no new objects
graphs.notes: One checkpoint delta, independent of source read position. Successful split publication and checkpoint application belong to the same metastore operation, not separate consensus protocols. Publication precedes SuggestTruncate. Restart reads acquired shard publish position. Notification failure does not undo checkpoint.

edges: immature uploaded split accepted by cache and directory renamed
successful put followed by non-cache scratch removal

another upload evicts cached split to make room and removal succeeds
graphs.notes: Path ownership, not filesystem crash-consistency model. Scratch Arc/parent references can retain directory until last owner. Cache rename/removal can fail and fail upload; cleanup failure does not imply successful removal. RAM serialization still produces disk-backed split before packaging. Cache fetch/move-out by merge and detailed cache registry/quota reconciliation are excluded.

edges: Source decodes Commit record or receives EOF for last non-EOF assigned shard
graphs.notes: Per-batch boolean changes the Indexer's enabled commit action. It is carried through RawDocBatch and ProcessedDocBatch. Commit testing occurs after the entire batch, not per document. New batches start ordinary. Indexer can already have extracted workbench for another threshold, making force-commit a no-op.

synchronous operation returns with batch/workbench still owned by Indexer
graphs.notes: Role-qualified dependency corresponding to shared thread_blocked execution. CPU instructions are running, not a wait. No CPU-time cutoff or inferred offload. Intrinsic Tantivy worker scheduling is excluded.

graphs.notes: Role-specific retained ownership differs from Indexer. Serialize CPU work uses running and these synchronous calls can use thread_blocked. No async per-builder scheduling state is introduced.

file operation returns with indexed/package batch scratch ownership retained
graphs.notes: Async method signature supplies no offload and no mandatory yield. Packaging CPU sections remain running. One dependency class covers synchronous file operations under the same owner rather than splitting every helper function.

metadata operation returns to payload preparation or its error path
graphs.notes: Distinct from later remote put/local streaming and cache filesystem offload dependencies. Synchronous metadata does not pre-open one file handle per payload. Allocation and SDK/library locks are not separately enumerated.

startup permit acquired and constructors/spawns run while permit is held

Processor/Serializer/Sequencer handles are dropped without explicit join here. No timeout and no detached-upload barrier. Ingest-v2 source construction has no internal await; unbounded Source assignment send supplies no capacity wait. Other configured-source load IO is excluded from this ingest-v2 census.

edges: startup permit acquired; fresh child switch and first stage actors spawned
all eight actors spawned and initial assignment admitted; install handles and increment generation
constructor/send error drops startup locals and schedules retry without explicit joined rollback
health FailureOrUnhealthy kills generation and takes handles
five selected kill/join futures complete; schedule retry

Healthy supervision tick requests observations and schedules next tick
graphs.notes: The custom IndexingPipeline directly owns eight handles, not generic Supervisor<A>. Partially spawned children can already execute before handles installation. Retry delay is min(2^retry_count seconds,600s); startup error schedules retry_count+1, running-generation failure schedules retry_count=0 after 1s. Shared timers carry retry count. Tick interval is 1s; progress checks gated by HEARTBEAT. Finalize only refreshes observations and never calls terminate. Generic Quit/kill/panic lifecycle remains in shared graph. NotFound startup exit branch is documented but not counted as a reachable additional ingest-v2 constructor path.
